_comment: The interpretive prose on the insights page. Numbers on the page regenerate
from PostHog every run; these sentences do not. `writtenFor` records the data
range they were written against — when the data moves past it, the build
prints a warning naming this file. Re-read the copy and bump the range.
Any {{token}} is substituted with a computed stat (see STAT_TOKENS in
scripts/insights.mjs), so prefer a token over typing a number by hand.
title: cdg2mp4 — first month of data
headline: The first month of actually knowing
lede: For seven years the only signal this tool produced was email when it broke. Analytics went live on {{rangeFromLong}}. Here is every number it has recorded since, including the ones that flatter the project less than the headline does.
cumNote: The curve is flat for most of the period and then turns almost vertical at the end. That is not a marketing win. It is a handful of people discovering they can feed the tool an entire disc collection.
dailyNote: Three spikes carry the month: {{topDays}}. Each is one person working through a library.
idsNote: Arrivals are steady and roughly linear, unlike conversions. New people keep showing up at about the same rate whether or not a power user is mid-binge.
caveatNote: PostHog identifies anonymous visitors with a per-browser ID kept in local storage, and this app never calls identify, so nothing is ever merged across devices. One ID means one browser profile that has not cleared its storage. It does not mean one person. Every ID is a UUIDv7, so the creation time can be decoded: the median gap between an ID being minted and its first event is half a second, confirming a fresh ID per new browser profile rather than per human.
breakdownNote: Sorted by how much they tell you. Only the first row represents anyone who used the tool for its purpose.
breakdownAfter: Even {{converted}} overstates it. Same-city, same-OS profiles created minutes apart show up repeatedly: the heaviest user in Florida appears as two profiles totalling 291 conversions, and Lima, Medellín and Tlaxcala each show a pair. A realistic count of humans who have completed a conversion is closer to 35 than to {{profiles}}.
failNote: {{failed}} failures across {{started}} attempts. Most days are zero. The clusters are not random.
calloutTitle: One machine has never once succeeded
calloutBody: Two browser profiles in the same Mexican city, created 32 minutes apart, have tried 18 times across four visits since July 4 and failed every time inside 3 seconds. Firefox names the cause: v128 not enabled, the WebAssembly SIMD type the ffmpeg core requires. Chrome 109 and Firefox 115 are the last versions available on Windows 7, 8 and 8.1, so upgrading is not available to them.

They retried, toggled offline storage, switched themes, and opened the feedback form twice. The app told them to “try again”, which will never work on that hardware. Filed as issue #75: detect the missing capability up front and offer the command-line fallback instead.
footer: Events are anonymous: no accounts, no file contents, no identities. Filenames and coarse IP geolocation are recorded; the conversion itself runs entirely in the browser. “Self” traffic is my own testing; “datacenter” is bot and scanner traffic from cloud regions. Generated {{generatedOn}} from data through {{rangeToLong}}.
